subject: Equinox Health: throughput spike & 5xx surge — executive lifeguard comms
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@equinoxhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@equinoxhealth.com>, Michael Kang <m.kang@equinoxhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate + throughput drop affecting Equinox prod since 08:45 PT

Irene —

We're seeing a sudden jump in 5xx errors and end-to-end latency across our Equinox production traffic starting ~08:45 PT. Throughput is throttling back (approx -40% RPS) and some customer-facing flows are timing out.

Key notes: 
- Errors: spike in 503/504s and increased token-generation time for chat endpoints.
- Timeline: looks correlated with a Redwood deployment (your side) around 08:40 PT per our tracing.
- Impact: intermittent failures for payment-authorize and patient-notes sync; our ops team is getting paged.

Attaching a short telemetry excerpt. Can you confirm whether a model swap or routing change was pushed at your end? We need an immediate point of contact and the expected ETA for mitigation. This is affecting active customer journeys — assigning priority.

Attachments: equinox_telemetry_excerpt_1020.csv (attached)

Jordan
Director, Platform Reliability
Equinox Health
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@equinoxhealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Bcc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:18:34 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate + throughput drop affecting Equinox prod since 08:45 PT

Jordan — thank you for the alert and the telemetry. We see the same signals in our surface metrics. I'm standing up an exec-level lifeguard bridge now and will coordinate updates.

Immediate ask from our side:
- Can you forward full request-id list for 09:00–09:20 PT (sample of 20) so we can trace tokenization/KV behavior?
- We'll start a fallback routing to a compatible model variant to stabilize traffic within the next 12 minutes; I'll confirm when that's active.

I've looped in David (ops lead) and Monica (CS lead). David — please get Karthik on a KV/cache triage and request-routing change. Monica — I'll need a customer-facing one-pager in 30 minutes.

Irene Choi
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:22:10 -0700
Subject: RE: High error rate + throughput drop affecting Equinox prod since 08:45 PT

Team — quick triage notes and actions I kicked off: 
1) Confirmed a rolling rollout at 08:39 that included a micro-change to the model routing policy for tokenization-specialized prompts.
2) Karthik is running an immediate KV prefix flush for Equinox tenant scope and will push a routing rollback to the previous model variant (v2.3.1 -> v2.3.0) as a mitigation.
3) Decreased default batch size for Equinox production to minimize per-token latencies while we assess.

Attachments I pushed to this thread: kv-cache-dump-10-20.txt (sample), snippet-error-503.log (selected spans).

Karthik — update when the KV flush and routing rollback complete and include commands executed. I'll monitor ingress/egress at the cluster level.

-David
Senior Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:29:57 -0700
Subject: RE: High error rate + throughput drop affecting Equinox prod since 08:45 PT

On Tue, Oct 20, 2026 at 09:22 AM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Karthik — update when the KV flush and routing rollback complete and include commands executed. I'll monitor ingress/egress at the cluster level.

Done with the first wave. Summary: 
- KV prefix flush completed for tenant eqx-prod (commands: infractl kv flush --tenant eqx-prod --prefix conv_cache --confirm).
- Rolled routing back to model v2.3.0 for the primary inference tier (rollback command: infractl routing update --tenant eqx-prod --from v2.3.1 --to v2.3.0 --force).
- Reduced batch_size from 32 -> 16 on the live pool to reduce tail latency.

Observations (engineer notes):
- Error pattern shows tokenization blowups on a small set of long prompts (~0.6% of traffic) that cause severe KV cache churn and lead to transient 503s under high concurrency.
- After rollback + KV flush, 503s dropped by ~65% in the first 3 minutes and P95 latency improved ~220ms. Still monitoring for full recovery.

Attaching: snippet-error-503.log (selected entries). Next: we'll bring up a hotfix to the tokenizer heuristics if bounce continues.

-Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@equinoxhealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:38:05 -0700
Subject: Equinox: immediate status and customer-facing summary

Jordan — quick update for your ops and product teams: 
- What we saw: model-routing change coincident with tokenization-heavy prompts caused KV churn -> transient 503 errors and throughput drop.
- What we did (first 20 minutes): KV prefix flush, routing rollback to v2.3.0, lowered batch sizes.
- Current impact: 503s down ~65% from peak; throughput returning toward baseline but a small percentage of long-prompt requests still see elevated latency.
- ETA: we expect full stabilization in 45–60 minutes barring new traffic patterns.

Customer-facing commitments we propose: 
- Ongoing live updates on this thread every 30 minutes until fully stabilised.
- Postmortem and timelines for tokenization heuristics hotfix within 48 hours.
- Offer: one-time service credit for affected window while we finalize root cause and remediation.

Would you like the one-pager as a short PDF to share with your execs?

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@equinoxhealth.com>

- Please confirm expected time window for the stabilization ETA (you mentioned 45–60m) and whether rolling back traffic to a lower concurrency will be required on our side.
- We will log a formal SLA credit request. Can you confirm the owner and the process?

Also copying our VP of Engineering (Michael) who may want a brief exec sync after stabilization.

Priya Rao

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@equinoxhealth.com>, Priya Rao <priya@equinoxhealth.com>, Michael Kang <m.kang@equinoxhealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Equinox stabilization summary + executive next steps and credit proposal

Team — final executive update after 24-hour observation window. Summary: 
- Timeline: initial spike 2026-10-20 08:45 PT; mitigation (KV flush + routing rollback + reduced batch size) applied 09:29 PT. Full customer-facing traffic stabilization achieved by 10:10 PT.
- Root cause: a targeted routing change inadvertently routed a small population of long prompts to a tokenizer-heavy model variant, causing KV churn and transient 5xxs under high concurrency.
- Impact: intermittent failures and throughput reduction for ~27 minutes at peak; we recorded a P95 latency regression up to +420ms for the affected requests.

Actions taken: 
- Immediate: KV flush, routing rollback, temporary batching reduction.
- Short term (24–48h): tokenizer heuristic patch and extended canary to validate.
- Postmortem: full incident report and code-level fix ETA by 2026-10-22 EOD; we will include mitigation timelines and tokenized request samples.

Customer remedies we propose (pending your approval): 
- One-time service credit equivalent to 10% of the September–October consumption during the impacted window (we can compute exact USD).
- A joint technical review next week with our research and serving runtime leads to walk through tokenization edge cases.

Monica — please prepare the credit estimate and the 1-page executive summary PDF; include the SLO impact chart (slo-impact-chart.png).
David/Karthik — please attach the final logs and the KV-dump excerpt to the postmortem link.

If that package is acceptable, I will escalate approval with Finance for the credit and schedule the technical review.

Irene Choi
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
